page.layout: Running head at top with page number at top right. One main text column. Right margin holds one marginal note ("Motus") beside the line "Motus Physicus". Catchword "&" at the foot right, below the rule.

main_text.p: ADhuc fuerunt principia natu-ralia : Affectiones sunt, quæ corpo-ribus naturalibus essentialiter constitutis, adjunguntur naturaliter, e-isque vel insunt vel adsunt.
Affectio corporis naturalis est communis vel propria. Cōmunis affectio est Mu-tabilitas & Finitas corporis.
Mutabilitas est, qua corpus mutati-oni est obnoxium.
Omne enim Physicum corpus est Mutabile, Mutari potest.
A mutabilitate Naturæ pendet Motus. Cum enim natura mutatur, moveri dicitur.

MotusMotus Physicus est affectio corporis naturalis, est [?]ἐντελέχεια corporis mobilis, qua mobile à movente profecta. Seu: Est ἐνέργεια moventis in mobile. Per motum tanquam per medium itur ad perfectionem: adeoque est itio, progressio, contentio ad rem, non res ipsa.

p.i: Motus dupliciter consideratur, 1. Ratione moventis, à quo fit motus, & est ἐνέργεια & effectus moventis in mobili.
Effectus, inquam, id est, naturalis effectio

page.notes: The first letter "A" is a decorative woodcut initial, joined to "Dhuc" as "ADhuc". The faint "c" before "Motus" at the start of the Motus Physicus line is uncertain and was left out. The Greek word "ἐντελέχεια" is only partly legible and is marked [?]. The line "Mu-tabilitas" and "naturalis" are as printed. Long s is written as plain s throughout (printed "eft" read as "est"). Faint show-through from the reverse page in the right margin and lower left was ignored.
